## The claim you are working on {#the-claim-you-are-working-on}

Five independent analysts reanalysed a claim made by the original author (OA) as part of the robustness study. The claim, as presented to all analysts, was:

> "…poor economic performances … decrease positive dimensions of EU framing" (Teney 2016, p. 619)

The published coefficient – the specific number that the Task 2 constraints pointed to – is:

> **Unemployment → cosmopolitan EU framing: b = −0.0034, t = −4.03, p < .001** (Table 3, Model 1)

This comes from a three-level random-intercept model using pooled Eurobarometer data (16 waves, 2004–2013, 27 EU countries).

---

## Which claim, and why {#which-claim}

The claim on the card is one of several that the paper makes. It is the first half of a two-part hypothesis, whose second sentence, "The effect is stronger on the materialist dimensions of EU framing" (p. 621), was not given to the analysts. The [background page](../../background.qmd#sec-questions) quotes the hypotheses of the paper in full. Choosing which sentence to replicate is the first specification decision of any replication, made before the estimand, the graph or the menu, usually by the people who wrote the card; the second sentence of the hypothesis needs a grouping of the scales that the data only half support, as the [measurement module](../../companion/measurement.qmd#sec-theory) shows. The workshop keeps to the card, so that its results can be set beside those of the five analysts.
